Note that elements after the first failure are not inspected, so a trailing null may go undetected when at least one earlier element has already failed. AnyFailed(params Result[]?) Returns bool true if any of the specified Results failed, otherwise false. Exceptions ArgumentNullException results is null. ArgumentException A null element is encountered before the first failure. Note that elements after the first failure are not inspected, so a trailing null may go undetected when at least one earlier element has already failed. Failure(string) Creates a failed Result with the specified error message. public static Result Failure(string errorMessage) Parameters errorMessage string The error message indicating the reason for failure. Returns Result A failed Result whose ErrorMessage is set to errorMessage. Exceptions ArgumentException errorMessage is null, empty, or whitespace. Flatten(params Result[]?) Takes zero or more Results and flattens them into a single Result. public static Result Flatten(params Result[]? results) Parameters results Result[] Zero or more Results to flatten Returns Result If all the Results were successful (or the array is empty) the return value is a successful Result. If one or more failed, the return value is a failed Result and the ErrorMessage property will contain the errors from each failed Result separated by a newline character. Exceptions ArgumentNullException results is null. ArgumentException results contains a null element. Success() Creates a successful Result. public static Result Success() Returns Result A successful Result. Remarks Returns a cached singleton instance. Result is immutable, so reusing the same instance is safe and avoids per-call allocations on hot paths. Callers must not rely on reference identity to distinguish results: every call to Success() returns the same object, so two successful results will be reference-equal.

api/Wolfgang.TryPattern.Try.html.summary: Class Try Namespace Wolfgang.TryPattern Assembly Wolfgang.TryPattern.dll Provides methods to execute actions and functions with automatic exception handling returning a Result representing the outcome of the action/function and the return value of the function if successful or an error message if the action/function failed. public static class Try Inheritance object Try Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Methods Run(Action?) Executes the specified action, catching any exception that may occur. public static Result Run(Action? action) Parameters action Action The action to execute. Returns Result A Result that indicates if the action was successful. Exceptions ArgumentNullException action is null. RunAsync(Action?, CancellationToken) Executes the specified action asynchronously, catching any exception that may occur. public static Task<Result> RunAsync(Action? action, CancellationToken token = default) Parameters action Action The action to execute. token CancellationToken A CancellationToken that is passed to Run(Action, CancellationToken). If cancellation is requested before action begins executing, the task is canceled and an OperationCanceledException is propagated to the caller rather than wrapped in a failed Result. Once action has started, Run(Action, CancellationToken) cannot interrupt it; cancellation during execution is only observed if action itself cooperatively checks the token (e.g. via ThrowIfCancellationRequested()) and throws. Returns Task<Result> A Task of Result representing the asynchronous operation. Exceptions ArgumentNullException action is null. OperationCanceledException Cancellation was observed via token (either before action started, or because action itself observed the token and threw). RunAsync<T>(Func<Task<T?>>?, CancellationToken) Executes the specified asynchronous function, catching any exception that may occur. public static Task<Result<T?>> RunAsync<T>(Func<Task<T?>>? function, CancellationToken token = default) Parameters function Func<Task<T>> The asynchronous function to execute. token CancellationToken A CancellationToken that is checked before function is invoked. If cancellation is already requested, an OperationCanceledException is thrown without invoking function. The token is not threaded into function itself; if you need cancellation inside the function, capture the token in the lambda's closure. If function observes the token during execution (e.g. via Delay(int, CancellationToken)) and the resulting OperationCanceledException escapes, it is also propagated to the caller rather than wrapped in a failed Result<T>. Returns Task<Result<T>> A Task of Result<T> representing the asynchronous operation. Type Parameters T The return type of the function. Exceptions ArgumentNullException function is null. OperationCanceledException token was already canceled when this method was called, or function observed cancellation during execution and let an OperationCanceledException escape. Run<T>(Func<T>?) Executes the specified function and returns its result, catching any exception that may occur. public static Result<T?> Run<T>(Func<T>? function) Parameters function Func<T> The function to execute. Returns Result<T> A successful Result<T> wrapping the function's return value, or a failed Result<T> whose ErrorMessage is the caught exception's message. Type Parameters T The return type of the function. Exceptions ArgumentNullException function is null.

docs/getting-started.html.title: Getting Started | Wolfgang.TryPattern Documentation
docs/getting-started.html.summary: Getting Started Prerequisites .NET 10 SDK or later (required to build and test this repository, because the library multi-targets .NET 10.0) Any project targeting .NET Framework 4.6.2+, .NET Standard 2.0, .NET 8.0, or .NET 10.0 Installation Package Manager Console Install-Package Wolfgang.TryPattern .NET CLI dotnet add package Wolfgang.TryPattern PackageReference <PackageReference Include="Wolfgang.TryPattern" Version="0.3.1" /> Basic Usage Running an Action Use Try.Run to execute an action that might throw: using Wolfgang.TryPattern; var result = Try.Run(() => File.Delete(tempPath)); if (result.Failed) { Console.WriteLine($"Could not delete file: {result.ErrorMessage}"); } Running a Function Use Try.Run<T> to execute a function and capture its return value: var result = Try.Run(() => int.Parse(userInput)); if (result.Succeeded) { Console.WriteLine($"Parsed value: {result.Value}"); } else { Console.WriteLine($"Invalid input: {result.ErrorMessage}"); } Async Operations Both Action and Func<Task<T>> have async counterparts: var result = await Try.RunAsync( () => httpClient.GetStringAsync(url) ); if (result.Succeeded) { ProcessResponse(result.Value); } Async operations support cancellation: var result = await Try.RunAsync( () => httpClient.GetStringAsync(url), cancellationToken ); Note OperationCanceledException is intentionally not caught by Try.RunAsync. Cancellation propagates normally so callers can distinguish between a failed operation and a cancelled one. Composing Results When you need to run multiple operations and check the overall outcome: var result1 = Try.Run(() => ValidateName(name)); var result2 = Try.Run(() => ValidateEmail(email)); var result3 = Try.Run(() => ValidateAge(age)); // Check if any failed if (Result.AnyFailed(result1, result2, result3)) { Console.WriteLine("Validation errors occurred."); } // Or flatten into a single result with combined error messages var combined = Result.Flatten(result1, result2, result3); if (combined.Failed) { // ErrorMessage contains all failure messages joined by newlines Console.WriteLine(combined.ErrorMessage); } Creating Results Directly You can also create Result objects directly for your own methods: public Result ValidateOrder(Order order) { if (order.Items.Count == 0) { return Result.Failure("Order must contain at least one item."); } return Result.Success(); } public Result<decimal> CalculateDiscount(Order order) { if (order.Total < 50) { return Result<decimal>.Failure("Minimum order for discount is $50."); } return Result<decimal>.Success(order.Total * 0.10m); } Next Steps Browse the API Reference for complete method signatures and XML documentation View the source code on GitHub

docs/introduction.html.title: Introduction | Wolfgang.TryPattern Documentation
docs/introduction.html.summary: Introduction Wolfgang.TryPattern is a lightweight .NET library that brings structured error handling to your codebase through the Try pattern. It replaces scattered try/catch blocks with a clean, composable API that makes error handling explicit and predictable. The Problem Traditional .NET error handling relies on try/catch blocks that can obscure control flow, make it difficult to compose operations, and lead to inconsistent error handling across a codebase: string content; try { content = File.ReadAllText(path); } catch (Exception ex) { // Now what? Log? Return null? Throw a different exception? logger.LogError(ex, "Failed to read file"); return null; } The Solution Wolfgang.TryPattern wraps operations in Try.Run and returns a Result object that clearly communicates the outcome: var result = Try.Run(() => File.ReadAllText(path)); if (result.Succeeded) { Console.WriteLine(result.Value); } else { Console.WriteLine($"Error: {result.ErrorMessage}"); } Core Types Try A static class providing methods to execute actions and functions with automatic exception handling: Try.Run(Action) - Execute an action, returning a Result Try.Run<T>(Func<T>) - Execute a function, returning a Result<T> with the return value Try.RunAsync(Action, CancellationToken) - Execute an action asynchronously Try.RunAsync<T>(Func<Task<T>>, CancellationToken) - Execute an async function Result Represents the outcome of an operation: Succeeded - true if the operation completed without exceptions Failed - true if the operation threw an exception ErrorMessage - The exception message if the operation failed Result<T> Extends Result with a typed return value: Value - The return value from the function (throws InvalidOperationException if accessed on a failed result) Composition Helpers Result.Flatten(params Result[]) - Combine multiple results into one; if any failed, the error messages are joined Result.AnyFailed(params Result[]) - Check if any result in a set indicates failure Result.AllSucceeded(params Result[]) - Check if every result in a set indicates success Platform Support Wolfgang.TryPattern targets multiple frameworks for broad compatibility: Target Version .NET Framework 4.6.2+ .NET Standard 2.0 .NET 8.0, 10.0

docs/setup.html.summary: Setup Guide This guide provides instructions for setting up the Try Pattern library for development and usage. For Library Users Prerequisites .NET SDK (the library supports .NET Framework 4.6.2, .NET Standard 2.0, .NET 8.0, and .NET 10.0) Visual Studio 2022, VS Code, or Rider (recommended) Quick Setup Install via NuGet dotnet add package Wolfgang.TryPattern Add using statement using Wolfgang.TryPattern; Start using the library var result = await Try.RunAsync(() => SomeOperationAsync()); For Contributors Prerequisites .NET 8.0 SDK or later (for building the library which targets .NET 4.6.2 through .NET 10.0) Git Visual Studio 2022, VS Code, or Rider Clone the Repository git clone https://github.com/Chris-Wolfgang/Try-Pattern.git cd Try-Pattern Build the Solution dotnet restore dotnet build Run Tests dotnet test Project Structure Try-Pattern/ ├── src/ │ └── Wolfgang.TryPattern/ # Main library project ├── tests/ │ └── Wolfgang.TryPattern.Tests/ # Unit tests ├── examples/ │ ├── CSharp.DotNet8.Example/ # C# .NET 8 examples │ ├── CSharp.DotNet462.Example/ # C# .NET Framework examples │ ├── FSharp.DotNet8.Example/ # F# .NET 8 examples │ ├── FSharp.DotNet462.Example/ # F# .NET Framework examples │ ├── VB.DotNet8.Example/ # VB.NET .NET 8 examples │ └── VB.DotNet462.Example/ # VB.NET .NET Framework examples ├── benchmarks/ # Performance benchmarks └── docs/ # Documentation files Development Workflow 1. Building Documentation The project uses DocFX for documentation generation. cd docfx_project docfx build docfx serve Visit http://localhost:8080 to view the documentation. Running Examples Navigate to any example project and run: cd examples/CSharp.DotNet8.Example dotnet run Troubleshooting Build Errors Issue: Missing .NET SDK version Solution: Install the required .NET SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download Issue: NuGet package restore fails Solution: Clear NuGet cache and restore dotnet nuget locals all --clear dotnet restore Test Failures Issue: Tests fail on first run Solution: Ensure all dependencies are restored dotnet restore dotnet build dotnet test IDE Setup Visual Studio 2022 Open TryPattern.sln Restore NuGet packages (automatic) Build solution (Ctrl+Shift+B) Run tests (Ctrl+R, A) VS Code Open folder in VS Code Install C# extension Use integrated terminal for commands: dotnet build dotnet test Rider Open TryPattern.sln Restore NuGet packages (automatic) Build solution Run tests from Test Explorer Contributing Please read CONTRIBUTING.md for details on our code of conduct and the process for submitting pull requests.
